title: Million-Particle Systems on the GPU
subtitle: Transform Feedback & Compute Shaders
excerpt: Building high-performance particle systems using WebGL 2 transform feedback for physics simulation entirely on the GPU.

sections.content: Traditional CPU-based particle systems hit bottlenecks around 10-50k particles. By moving simulation to the GPU, we can render millions of particles at 60fps. This article explores WebGL 2 transform feedback - the key to stateful GPU computation in WebGL.

The system uses a ping-pong buffer pattern: read particle state from buffer A, write updated state to buffer B, then swap. Transform feedback captures vertex shader outputs directly to buffers without rasterization.

sections.title: Particle Simulation Vertex Shader
WebGL 2 Transform Feedback Configuration

sections.content: Always unbind transform feedback buffers before using them as vertex attributes! WebGL enforces no simultaneous read/write to the same buffer.

items: Memory: ~32 bytes per particle (position, velocity, life, color)

sections.content: The bottleneck shifts from simulation to rendering at high particle counts. Consider instanced billboard quads or point sprites with size attenuation for visual quality vs performance tradeoffs.
